condition: Lower-limb cellulitis with a portal of entry (DVT unlikely)
summary: 45-year-old woman with 2 days of spreading, well-demarcated, hot erythema of the left shin from a toe-web fissure (tinea); T 38.2, HR 96, no calf swelling. Eron class I-II: oral antibiotics; DVT not suspected.

inputs.hpi: Two days of a spreading red, hot, painful patch on the front of the left shin, started from cracked skin between the toes (athlete's foot). Feverish last night. No calf swelling, no recent travel or immobility. Seen previously for a sebaceous cyst.

exam.skin: Hot, tender, well-demarcated erythema over the left anterior shin (10 x 8 cm), marked; macerated fissured 4th toe web with scaling (tinea pedis). No bullae, no crepitus.
exam.msk: Calves equal and soft, no pitting oedema.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Cellulitis of the left lower leg
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Cellulitis left shin, Eron class I-II, portal of entry tinea pedis; DVT unlikely (no swelling, no risk factors): oral flucloxacillin, mark the edge, treat tinea, review at 48 hours.

emergencyLevel.note: Eron I-II cellulitis: outpatient oral antibiotics; an emergency redirect is over-triage.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: web.triage: emergency (acuity=urgent, action=emergency_now, score=48); expected ≤ urgent. Triage reasons: Systemic red flag symptom; Fever; Moderate pain score.
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: Tier fever without physiological derangement (NEWS2 <5) below emergency_now.

mustInclude.proposedFix: Map L03.11x (cellulitis of lower limb) to the cellulitis protocol in getProtocolByIcd; let the Assessment panel follow the confirmed diagnosis rather than the PANE top (cholecystitis 0.152 for a leg cellulitis).

mustExclude.note: DVT is not suspected (no swelling, no risk factors); empirical anticoagulation would be harm without benefit.

guideline.name: NICE NG141 - Cellulitis and erysipelas: antimicrobial prescribing
guideline.section: Exclude other causes of skin redness (e.g. inflammatory reaction, chronic venous insufficiency, DVT) before prescribing; cellulitis is usually unilateral; admit if severely unwell (Eron III-IV)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NG141. London: NICE; 2019.

guideline.name: NICE NG158 - Venous thromboembolic diseases: diagnosis, management and thrombophilia testing
guideline.section: 1.1 DVT: two-level Wells; likely -> proximal leg vein ultrasound within 4 h (interim anticoagulation if delayed); 1.1 PE: two-level Wells; likely (>4) -> CTPA immediately (interim anticoagulation if delayed); unlikely -> D-dimer; PERC when pre-test probability is low
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NG158. London: NICE; 2020 (updated 2023).

rationale: The other arm of the pair: true cellulitis with a clear portal of entry and no DVT features; checks for over-triage and unnecessary anticoagulation.
